newsitem.title: USA: Economist Gramlich emerges as likely Fed nominee.
newsitem.headline: Economist Gramlich emerges as likely Fed nominee.

text.p: University of Michigan economist Edward Gramlich is emerging as one of President Bill Clinton's likely nominees to the Federal Reserve Board, a U.S. official said on Thursday.

Two vacancies on the central bank's board opened up this year with the departure of Janet Yellen for the White House Council of Economic Advisers and Lawrence Lindsey for the conservative American Enterprise Institute think-tank.
The U.S. official, who declined to be identified, would not comment on potential candidates for the second position on the Federal Reserve Board, which sets U.S. monetary policy.

Gramlich, the dean of the University of Michigan's School of Public Policy, has been described as a top-flight economist whose research has ranged from poverty and income distribution to the economics of major league baseball.

He also has some Washington experience, having worked as the acting head of the Congressional Budget Office and having served as the chairman of a government advisory council that in January issued a report on ways to shore up the Social Security pension system.

White House spokesmen have declined comment on who Clinton might nominate to the Fed. Earlier on Thursday, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton was "satisfied" by the two potential nominees proposed to him by his staff but added it would probably take several weeks before the administration announced them.
